scope: Audit prepared before using any nl27 test outcomes; CPU float32 tiny models only. No real models, GPU jobs, cloud actions or LLM API calls.
checks: PASS: qa_split reads train only, loads plain originals without adapters, and calls the same letter_probs(..., solo) as bench_eval base; solo forces mode=zero so the bridge never exchanges states.

PASS: raw-original and disabled-adapter letter probabilities were bitwise identical on 16 real ARC/MMLU questions in tiny models; native model forward agrees. Both prefixes have 3 tokens and all four space-prefixed letters are single tokens in each tokenizer.

PASS: changing every gold answer left link, cut and shuffled pair probabilities bitwise unchanged. Text first-speaker probabilities are independent of gold; second-speaker scores use the first model prediction, not its gold label.
PASS: no-focus old/new train draw_any produced identical episodes and RNG states on 1000 draws each for pair, solo and text. FOCUS=None short-circuits the added RNG draw; defaults are unchanged.

PASS WITH QUALIFICATION: both nl27 arms share nl20 initialization, 300 steps, batch size 16, learning rate schedule and focus distribution. Pair consumes two additional selection RNG draws so actual question sequences differ. Half is the explicit focus mixture component; uniform draws may also hit exclusive questions. Pair/solo prompts differ, and pair retains the send-cost regularizer; this is a trained-system comparison.

PASS: pair/avg and ensemble both take argmax of the arithmetic mean of two four-letter softmax distributions, not averages of binary correctness or raw logits. pair/zero/avg reuses pair adapters, prompts and pooling with the link cut.

PASS WITH QUALIFICATION: D is chosen on solo validation before testing and is sensible for the old single-answerer analysis; it never enters either pooled comparison. Validation has 7 inputs repeated from train and 1 repeated into test, so D is not selected on a fully clean validation split.

FAIL HELD-OUT CLAIM: train/val/test have 16631/595/3165 rows; the row split is disjoint but question content is not. Train-test has 62 exact stem pairs involving 50 test questions, including 27 fully identical inputs and labels, plus one extra input differing only by punctuation spacing. All 28 full-input overlaps are MMLU.

NEAR MATCH SCREEN: exhaustive symbol-preserving character-5-gram Jaccard >=0.8 gives 249 nonidentical train-test stem pairs involving 101 test rows; many are shared passages or template variants with different answers, not proven duplicate questions. A separate val-test near screen finds 7 pairs/6 test rows.

FAIL IID/UNIQUE ASSUMPTION: 2 test rows repeat earlier complete inputs (case/format normalized). Exact-input sensitivity removes 31 rows total (28 training overlaps, 1 validation overlap, 2 within-test repeats), leaving 3134; broader stem/near sensitivity removes 153, leaving 3012. Near screen cannot exclude all semantic paraphrases.

PASS LIMITED CHECK: current coread training data has only generic-stem matches to benchmark test; none have the same choices. This is not a provenance proof for nl20 or a base pretraining contamination audit.

PASS P-VALUE / FAIL INTERVAL LABEL: two-sided exact McNemar p and point differences are correct. Scaling the conditional discordant-split interval by observed discordance is not an unconditional 95% accuracy-difference interval. Exact N=10,p10=.2,p01=0 coverage is 0.6241124352, unchanged without rounding; zero discordance spuriously returns [0,0].

REPORTING TRAP: test.all.headline and pair_beats_all retain the single-answerer analysis; pair_beats_all excludes ensemble and includes text. nl27 must read test.all.pooled, with positive differences and p<.05 for BOTH ensemble and pair/zero/avg. This conjunctive claim needs no multiple-comparator correction; choosing a winning endpoint/subgroup does.

TEXT ARM UNMATCHED: nl23 text_step_300 uses no focus; neither pooled endpoint uses text, so primary results are unaffected, but text comparisons and pair_beats_all cannot be called focus-matched. Text training teacher-forces the first correct letter, encouraging copying; it is not a general test of deliberative text collaboration.

FIGURE COMPATIBILITY: figures/capability.py at 7eb277f expects the old arm set and old single-answerer headline; it rejects the additional pooled arms. Do not present its old plots as nl27 pooling results.

PASS SMOKE: qa_split on 128 real training questions gave tiny exclusive sets Quill 38 and Ember 30; initialization and focused pair/solo training, focused and unfocused text training, and 8-question bench_eval completed with heads=2, head_dim=16, xblocks=1,2,4. Separate scoring checks included 8 ARC and 8 MMLU questions.

PASS EXISTING TESTS: exact-commit snapshot, pytest test_link.py test_stream.py test_chain.py test_pause.py test_pen.py test_leakage.py test_coldstart.py test_stats.py: 15 passed, 2 skipped, 2 subtests passed; collection-time standalone link/stream/pause/pen/coldstart assertions also executed. Skips require external trained checkpoint or archive inputs.

PASS NEW TESTS: exact multinomial enumeration at five distributions gives >=95% CI coverage; sparse near matches equal brute-force set comparison on 42 positive real pairs; real tiny score reanalysis preserves McNemar p/point differences, applies exclusions and rejects mismatched/truncated result files.

PASS PROPOSED PATCH: ran bench_eval with the proposed CI wrapper in the isolated snapshot; all 19 per-question correctness vectors, accuracies, answerer, pooled discordant counts, point differences and p-values equal the unpatched run. End-to-end --scores CLI reanalysis on the real tiny output also passed.

bugs_and_effects.bug: Content leakage and repeated test inputs in build_bench output
bugs_and_effects.effect: The original all/MMLU accuracies, pooled comparisons and per-question inference cannot be described as wholly unseen/unique-question results. This does not prove the headline direction is wrong; outcomes must be recomputed after exclusions. Not every eligible duplicate was necessarily sampled in 4800 training draws. ARC has no full-input duplicates here, but has 12 broader stem/near flags.
bugs_and_effects.fix: New offline reanalysis applies outcome-independent exact-input and broader lexical sensitivity masks to the existing per_question vectors. It preserves all original outputs and training indices; the original data generator is unchanged. For future builds, deduplicate or group related questions before splitting.

bugs_and_effects.bug: Conditional interval presented as a population accuracy-difference interval
bugs_and_effects.effect: All legacy lo/hi fields in pooled, vs_pair and headline lack the advertised unconditional coverage. Accuracy, n10/n01, diff and exact McNemar p do not change merely because of this interval fix.
bugs_and_effects.fix: New offline paired() uses a conservative 95% Bonferroni difference of two 97.5% exact marginal Clopper-Pearson intervals. No existing measured function was changed. A small proposed bench_eval diff is included below, not applied because git diff origin/main -- pairing/bench_eval.py is nonempty.

confusion_resolved: I notice I’m confused: qa_split.py was absent and nl27 additions missing from working train.py/bench_eval.py. origin/main and commit 7eb277f do contain them; the shared working files differ. Audited a git archive snapshot of the exact commit instead of overwriting shared edits.

I notice I’m confused: a nominal 95% accuracy-difference interval covered only 62.4% in an exact example. Enumerated all binomial outcomes and repeated without rounding: 0.6241124352. The failure is treating the observed discordance fraction as fixed; the p-value remains valid.

I notice I’m confused: an unfocused-text smoke retry could no longer open in27/replies.json although earlier runs succeeded. That transient input path had disappeared. Copied the real nl20 replies to the temporary snapshot and reran successfully; no replacement data were invented.

limitations: One training seed; question-level significance is conditional on these checkpoints. Probability scoring conditions on the fixed answer prefix and A-D, not unconstrained free generation. Pair-vs-ensemble compares two trained systems with different prompts; pair-vs-cut isolates acute link use but does not alone establish better learning or knowledge beyond the bases. No nl27 test results were inspected.
